questions.question: A car wheel rotates on which product?
questions.explanation: Hub unit bearings combine bearing, flange and often a sensor to support each wheel.

questions.question: Car AC compressor clutch uses which bearing?
questions.explanation: Magnetic clutch bearings support the AC compressor pulley; NSK Chennai makes them.

questions.question: Gearbox shafts are supported by?
questions.explanation: Transmission bearings (ball, tapered and needle) carry gear loads inside the gearbox.

questions.question: Differential pinion usually uses which type?
questions.explanation: Tapered roller bearings take heavy combined radial and axial gear loads.

questions.question: Engine belt idler pulleys use which bearing?
questions.explanation: Sealed single or double-row ball bearings run idler and tensioner pulleys.

questions.question: EPS in cars stands for?
questions.explanation: Electric Power Steering uses a motor instead of hydraulics, improving fuel economy.

questions.question: ABS sensor at the hub unit reads what?
questions.explanation: A magnetic encoder in the hub seal lets the ABS sensor read wheel speed.

questions.question: Low-friction hub seals help the vehicle with?
questions.explanation: Lower seal drag cuts energy loss, improving fuel economy or EV driving range.

questions.question: Needle bearings are chosen when space is?
questions.explanation: Needle rollers carry high radial load in a very small cross-section.

questions.question: EV e-axle bearings must resist what?
questions.explanation: Inverter currents can pass through e-axle bearings, so insulated designs are used.

questions.question: An RFQ from a car maker asks for?
questions.explanation: A Request for Quotation invites NSK to quote price, capacity and timing for a new part.

questions.question: SOP in auto projects means?
questions.explanation: SOP is the date mass production for the vehicle programme begins.

questions.question: A nomination letter from an OEM means?
questions.explanation: A nomination letter confirms NSK has won the part for a vehicle programme.

questions.question: PPAP approval is needed before?
questions.explanation: PPAP proves the part and process meet all OEM requirements before serial supply.

questions.question: Quality standard required by auto OEMs?
questions.explanation: IATF 16949 is the automotive quality management standard required by most OEMs.

questions.question: Yearly price cut in long contracts is called?
questions.explanation: OEMs often ask for yearly price-downs in long-term deals, offset by VA/VE savings.

questions.question: VA/VE aims to do what?
questions.explanation: Value Analysis/Value Engineering removes cost while keeping function and quality.

questions.question: A Tier-1 supplier sells directly to?
questions.explanation: Tier-1 suppliers supply the OEM directly; Tier-2 suppliers supply the Tier-1s.

questions.question: Standard customer complaint report?
questions.explanation: An 8D gives containment, root cause, permanent fix and prevention in eight disciplines.

questions.question: Supplier quality at OEMs is measured in?
questions.explanation: PPM (defective parts per million) is the key OEM quality metric for suppliers.

questions.question: OTIF stands for?
questions.explanation: OTIF measures orders delivered on the promised date in the full quantity.

questions.question: An OEM line stop caused by late parts brings?
questions.explanation: Line stoppages are very costly, so OEMs charge suppliers for delays they cause.

questions.question: EDI with OEMs is used for?
questions.explanation: Electronic Data Interchange sends delivery schedules and ship notices system-to-system.

questions.question: ASN in OEM supply stands for?
questions.explanation: An ASN tells the customer what was shipped and when, before the truck arrives.

questions.question: Fixed near-term part of an OEM schedule is?
questions.explanation: Within the frozen window quantities are fixed so supply can be planned reliably.

questions.question: Main job of a key account manager?
questions.explanation: KAMs own the relationship, forecasts, pricing and growth with a major customer.

questions.question: Best first reply to a customer complaint?
questions.explanation: Fast acknowledgement and containment build trust while the root cause is found.

questions.question: A warranty claim means the part failed?
questions.explanation: Warranty claims arise when parts fail in customers' vehicles during the warranty period.

questions.question: OEM supplier scorecards rate mainly?
questions.explanation: OEM scorecards track PPM, delivery, response time and cost to grade suppliers.

questions.question: Containment action in an 8D aims to?
questions.explanation: Containment (D3) quickly isolates suspect stock so no more bad parts reach the customer.

questions.question: Steel price swings are shared through?
questions.explanation: Raw-material index clauses adjust part prices in line with published steel indices.

questions.question: Selling price minus variable cost is?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin shows how much each sale covers fixed costs and profit.

questions.question: A cost breakdown sheet shows the OEM?
questions.explanation: Cost breakdowns split material, process, overhead and margin for price discussions.

questions.question: DSO measures what?
questions.explanation: Days Sales Outstanding shows how long customers take to pay invoices.

questions.question: One-time tooling cost is often recovered by?
questions.explanation: Tooling may be paid separately or amortised into the part price over agreed volumes.

questions.question: India's largest car maker by volume?
questions.explanation: Maruti Suzuki has long held the largest share of India's passenger car market.

questions.question: Chennai's auto hub nickname is?
questions.explanation: Chennai hosts many vehicle and component plants, earning the 'Detroit of Asia' name.

questions.question: Aftermarket means sales of?
questions.explanation: Aftermarket parts replace worn components in vehicles already on the road.

questions.question: Typical car model production life?
questions.explanation: Nominated parts usually supply for the model life, often around five to seven years.

questions.question: Two-wheelers use bearings in wheels and?
questions.explanation: Bikes use bearings in wheels, steering, crankshaft and transmission.

questions.question: NSK suffix 'DDU' means?
questions.explanation: DDU is NSK's code for contact rubber seals on both sides.

questions.question: Sealed bearings normally need relubrication?
questions.explanation: Sealed bearings come pre-greased and normally need no relubrication.

questions.question: False brinelling often happens during?
questions.explanation: Small vibrations without rotation, as in shipping, wear marks at rolling contacts.

questions.question: Why do OEMs want lighter bearings?
questions.explanation: Lower weight cuts vehicle energy use and emissions.

questions.question: A ball screw converts rotation into?
questions.explanation: Ball screws turn rotary motor motion into precise straight-line movement, as in EPS.

questions.question: NSK's first India venture (1997) made?
questions.explanation: NSK began in Chennai in 1997 via Rane Nastech, making steering columns and joints.

questions.question: NSK Chennai bearing plant opened in?
questions.explanation: The NSK-ABC bearing plant near Chennai held its opening ceremony in February 2008.

questions.question: NSK Chennai plant is located in?
questions.explanation: The plant is in a SIPCOT industrial park in Kancheepuram district near Chennai.

questions.question: Rane NSK's Gujarat plant makes what?
questions.explanation: Rane NSK Steering Systems opened a Gujarat plant at Changodar in 2018 to make EPS.

questions.question: NSK's global headquarters is in?
questions.explanation: NSK Ltd. is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.
